samples.summary: `docStore.snapshot()` is called outside the new `doc.batch(...)`, producing two undo checkpoints for one in-place link edit (and wiping redo on a no-op edit)
samples.evidence: editor.ts:3620 does `docStore.snapshot();` and then, at 3641, `doc.batch(() => {...})`. `MemDocStore.snapshot()` (store/memory.ts:177) pushes an undo checkpoint when `batchDepth === 0`, and `MemDocStore.batch()` (memory.ts:206-209) unconditionally pushes a *second* clone of the same state before running the body. Result: two identical checkpoints for one operation, so the second Cmd+Z (and the first Cmd+Y) appears to do nothing — exactly the failure mode the repo already documents and fixed elsewhere (editor.ts:1218-1222, where `withNamedStyleChange` deliberately puts `docStore.snapshot()` INSIDE `doc.batch`). Worse, when the new URL equals the old href the batch body is a net no-op: `batch()`'s `wroteNothing` path restores `priorRedo` and pops its own checkpoint, but the outer `snapshot()` has already cleared `redoStack` and left a dead undo entry, so re-applying the same URL silently destroys the redo stack. The same pattern is duplicated at packages/docs/src/view/text-box-editor.ts:1202/1212, where the store is always `MemDocStore`. The new test only presses undo once, so it does not catch this.

samples.summary: Apply guard checks only that *some* link is at the caret, so a caret that moved into a different link makes Apply rewrite the wrong link
samples.evidence: `if (editingExistingLink && !editor.getLinkAtCursor()) { … return; }` (docs-link-popover.tsx:152) tests only for the presence of any link at the caret, not that it is the link the popover was opened on (`editUrl`'s original href / `linkInfo.href`). The popover deliberately stays open when the caret leaves the link, so clicking into a *different* hyperlink and pressing Apply passes the guard and `editor.insertLink(url)` takes editor.ts's in-place branch (editor.ts:3617-3667), rewriting the href — and now, with `linkTextFollowsHref` true, the visible text — of a link the user never meant to edit.

samples.summary: Apply silently discards the user's typed URL when the caret has left the link
samples.evidence: The new branch calls `editor.focus(); close(); return;` without applying anything and without any feedback. The user typed a URL and pressed Apply/Enter; the popover just vanishes and nothing happens, which is indistinguishable from a broken button. It also blocks the previously working case of opening ⌘K on a link, then selecting other text and pressing Apply to link that selection (the old code would have gone through `insertLink`'s selection branch, editor.ts:3582).

samples.summary: Line affinity that `withOffset` deliberately drops is re-supplied by the caller, attaching an affinity computed for a different offset to the caret
samples.evidence: `withOffset` (link-run.ts:109-112) drops `lineAffinity` when it moves an endpoint, documented as 'dropping a now-stale wrap affinity'. But every caller then does `this.cursor.moveTo(snapped.focus, snapped.focus.lineAffinity ?? result.lineAffinity)` (text-editor.ts:2354-2357, and likewise 2017-2020 and 2068). `Cursor.moveTo` gives the explicit second argument priority (`affinity ?? pos.lineAffinity`, cursor.ts:55), so exactly when the focus was expanded the stale affinity of the *pre-expansion* offset is reinstated on the caret, while the stored selection endpoint carries none. At a wrap boundary this can paint the caret on the wrong visual line and makes cursor and selection endpoint disagree.

samples.summary: In-place link rewrite moves the caret but never sets `needsScrollIntoView`
samples.evidence: The sibling insert branch sets `needsScrollIntoView = true` before `render()` (editor.ts:3681) because it moves the caret after changing text length. The new in-place branch also moves the caret (`cursor.moveTo(... link.start + url.length)`, line 3660) after a text replacement that can change the block's wrapping, but calls `render()` without requesting scroll-into-view, so the caret can end up off-screen.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. editor.ts:3620 calls docStore.snapshot() outside the doc.batch(...) opened at editor.ts:3641; Doc.batch delegates to store.batch (document.ts:146-148); MemDocStore.snapshot() pushes an undo checkpoint and clears redoStack when batchDepth===0 (memory.ts:177-184), and MemDocStore.batch() then unconditionally pushes a second clone of the same state and clears redoStack again (memory.ts:206-209). One in-place link href edit therefore costs two identical undo checkpoints, making the second Cmd+Z a visible no-op. When the new URL equals the existing href the batch body is a net no-op, and the wroteNothing path (memory.ts:230-236) restores priorRedo — which is already [] because the outer snapshot() cleared it at line 183 — so the redo stack is silently destroyed and a dead undo entry is left. The repo's own withNamedStyleChange (editor.ts:1236-1245, with the explanatory comment at 1218-1222) puts docStore.snapshot() INSIDE doc.batch precisely to avoid this, confirming the intended contract. The same ordering is duplicated at text-box-editor.ts:1202/1212. No guard makes this unreachable: snapshot()'s only suppression is batchDepth > 0, and the batch has not been entered at the call site. Broken undo invariant plus redo-history loss on a reachable path is in the correctness lane and blocking at major severity.

mergedFrom.summary: Apply silently discards the user's typed URL when the caret has left the link
mergedFrom.evidence: The new branch calls `editor.focus(); close(); return;` without applying anything and without any feedback. The user typed a URL and pressed Apply/Enter; the popover just vanishes and nothing happens, which is indistinguishable from a broken button. It also blocks the previously working case of opening ⌘K on a link, then selecting other text and pressing Apply to link that selection (the old code would have gone through `insertLink`'s selection branch, editor.ts:3582).

verdict.reason: Verified in the repo. docs-link-popover.tsx:152 guards Apply with `editingExistingLink && !editor.getLinkAtCursor()`, which only tests that *some* href exists at the caret; it never compares to the link the popover was opened on (linkInfo.href set at :127, or editRequest.initialUrl at :86). The popover deliberately survives caret movement while in edit mode (:67, :72, :75) and has no outside-click/blur dismissal (only scroll :107, Escape :167, Apply), and docs-view.tsx:630-636 passes no close prop. So caret-into-a-different-link then Apply passes the guard, and editor.insertLink takes the collapsed-caret in-place branch (editor.ts:3617-3668), where findLinkRunAt resolves the link at the *current* caret and applyInlineStyle rewrites its href (:3642); with linkTextFollowsHref true (:3634, link-run.ts:67) it also inserts the URL and deletes the old run text (:3647-3651). Result: href and visible text of an unintended link are overwritten on a normally reachable editing path — a correctness/data-overwrite defect, major.
